name: Sortivo Tabs Organizer
author: mbenneke

sections.description:
The Plugins page is one long list, and every plugin adds its own item to the admin menu. Sortivo Tabs Organizer organizes your plugins into tabs like SEO, Security, Speed & Cache, Backup, Forms, Shop and more, and groups the admin menu the same way.

  • Automatic sorting – every plugin lands in the right tab the moment you activate Sortivo Tabs Organizer.
  • Move any plugin – a small “Tab” picker under each plugin lets you put it somewhere else, or back on Auto.
  • Your own tabs – make tabs like “Client X” or “To remove”.
  • Remembers your tab – after activating, deactivating or searching you stay in the tab you were in.
  • Tidy sidebar – the menu items plugins add to the left sidebar are grouped under the same tab names, with a collapsible header per group. No page is moved and no link changes, so every plugin keeps working. Turn it off with one checkbox on the Plugins page.
  • Arrange the sidebar yourself – click “Arrange menu” at the bottom of the sidebar, or “Arrange sidebar” at the top of the Plugins page. Drag groups up and down, and drag any menu item into a group, also WordPress’s own items like Posts or Settings. Make a new group for them, or reset everything with one click. Until you do this, nothing changes.
  • Export / import – download your layout as a file (Tools > Sortivo Tabs) and import it on other sites, or use WP-CLI: wp sortivo export and wp sortivo import.
  • Works with the All / Active / Inactive / Update filters and with search.

Sortivo Tabs Organizer does not send any data anywhere. Your layout is stored in your own database.
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard, go to Plugins > Add Plugin and search for “Sortivo Tabs Organizer”, or upload the zip file there.
  2. Activate it. The tabs appear on the Plugins page right away.
  3. Optional: move plugins to another tab with the “Tab” picker, or click “+ New tab” to make your own.
sections.faq:
Does it change or move my plugins?

No. It only changes how the Plugins list and the admin sidebar are shown. Plugins are not moved, renamed or changed. Deactivate Sortivo Tabs Organizer and everything looks exactly as before.

How does it decide which tab a plugin goes in?

Well-known plugins are recognised by their slug. Others are sorted by keywords in their name and description. If a plugin lands in the wrong tab, pick another tab under that plugin and it stays there.

Can I turn off the sidebar grouping?

Yes. Untick “Group the sidebar menu too” at the top of the Plugins page.

Can I move WordPress’s own menu items, like Posts or Settings?

Yes. Click “Arrange menu” at the bottom of the sidebar and drag them into a group, or click “+ New group” to make one for them. By default they stay where WordPress puts them. “Reset” in the same place puts the whole sidebar back to the default; your tabs stay.

Can I change the order of the groups?

Yes. In “Arrange menu”, drag a group header up or down. The tabs on the Plugins page follow the same order.

Can I use the same tabs on all my sites?

Yes. Go to Tools > Sortivo Tabs, download the export file and import it on your other sites. Plugins that are not installed there yet get their tab as soon as you install them. With WP-CLI: wp sortivo export > layout.json and wp sortivo import layout.json.

Does it slow down my site?

No. It only works in the admin area and adds nothing to the pages your visitors see.

Does it work with big plugins like WooCommerce?

Yes. It is tested with WooCommerce, Yoast SEO, Contact Form 7, UpdraftPlus, WP Mail SMTP and Complianz. All menu items of a plugin, like WooCommerce’s Products, Payments and Analytics, stay together in its group.

Does it work on multisite?

Multisite has not been tested yet, so it is not officially supported for now.
sections.changelog:
0.7.2

  • Fix: on some hosts an update did not fully take effect, because their server cache kept serving the old script and style of the plugin for days. The plugin now puts its small script and style into the admin page itself, so every update takes effect right away.
  • Fix: the “Arrange sidebar” link keeps its link style with themes that style all buttons.

0.7.1

  • Fix: after opening groups in the sidebar you can scroll down to the bottom of the menu again.
  • New: an “Arrange sidebar” link at the top of the Plugins page, next to “Group the sidebar menu too”.

0.7.0

  • New: “Arrange menu” at the bottom of the sidebar. Drag groups up and down, and drag any menu item into a group, also WordPress’s own items like Posts or Settings. The tabs on the Plugins page follow the same order.
  • New: make a new group while arranging, or reset the sidebar to its default layout.
  • The export file now includes the sidebar arrangement. Export files from older versions still import.

0.6.1

  • First public release on WordPress.org.
  • Fix: a sidebar group now folds away completely, also when another plugin (such as WooCommerce) adds its own separator inside it.
  • Fix: menu items without a page of their own, such as WooCommerce’s Payments and Products, now move along when you move their plugin to another tab.

0.6.0

  • First release.

The Plugins page split into tabs automatically, with the number of plugins in each tab.
Move any plugin to another tab with the "Tab" picker under it, or set it back to Auto.
